extracted.intended_audience: investigators applying for NIH R01 grants (NIH applicants) / institutional officials
extracted.subtask_description: Summary statement and explicit review criteria used by an NIH CSR Special Emphasis Panel to evaluate an R01 application, including the five scored criteria (Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, Environment) plus administrative and policy items (human/animal subjects, resource sharing, budget).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact (Impact Score / Percentile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact: (panel text describing the application's overall significance and likely influence). Impact Score: 10  Percentile: 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The impact/priority score is calculated after discussion of an application by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10. Some applications also receive a percentile ranking. Reviewers' overall impact comments summarize strengths and weaknesses and the panel's enthusiasm; example text: 'Overall, there is extremely high enthusiasm for this outstanding grant application.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance: (criterion score reported, here '1'). Assessment of whether the project addresses an important problem and the potential to advance understanding or have an important influence on the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel evaluates if the work is of high significance (examples of strengths: 'The identification of an inducible anti-viral and anti-fungal response in C. elegans... is of high significance'). Reviewers list specific strengths and any weaknesses (here: 'None noted').

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigator(s): (criterion score reported, here '1'). Assessment of the qualifications, track record, and appropriateness of the PI and key personnel to conduct the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider investigator's past contributions and current team's expertise; examples: 'Exceptional investigator who discovered the IPR and the role of Drh1...' and 'Excellent collaborators who provide complementary expertise.' Weaknesses should be noted if present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation: (criterion score reported). Assessment of whether the project employs novel concepts, approaches, or tools and how it challenges current paradigms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate novelty of discoveries and tools (examples: 'The discovery of the IPR and its antiviral sensor... are highly innovative'; 'identification of N-terminal domains resembling CARDs is novel'). Note any lack of innovation as weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach: (criterion score reported). Assessment of the experimental design, methods, analyses, consideration of rigor, and feasibility, including discussion of potential pitfalls and alternative approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel examines clarity and rigor of the experimental plan, appropriateness of methods, contingency plans, and whether approaches are too open-ended. Example strengths: 'Exceptionally well written and clear experimental plan', 'Careful attention to potential pitfalls and alternative approaches.' Example weaknesses: 'Some of the screens and mass spec approaches are open ended and may not yield new insights' and specific technical suggestions (e.g., consider C-terminal fusion to avoid interfering with function).

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Environment: (criterion score reported). Assessment of institutional support, available resources, and whether the environment is likely to contribute to success of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate intellectual and material environment; examples: 'The research environment is ideal for this project', 'Excellent resources both intellectual environment and material resources.' Note any environmental shortcomings if present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Human Subjects: determination of involvement of human subjects in the research (here: '10-No human subjects involved').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If human subjects are involved, reviewers assess protections, risk/benefit, inclusion, and consent; if none, record 'No human subjects involved'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Vertebrate Animals: determination of involvement and appropriateness of use of vertebrate animals (here: '10-No live vertebrate animals involved for competing appl.' and elsewhere 'Not Applicable (No Vertebrate Animals)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, reviewers assess justification, welfare, and adherence to policies. If not applicable, indicate as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Biohazards: assessment of biological hazards and containment considerations (examples in critiques: 'Not Applicable (No Biohazards)' and 'Orsay virus is BSL1').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers note whether proposed work involves biohazards and whether appropriate biosafety measures are described and acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource Sharing Plans: evaluation of plans for sharing data, reagents, and other resources (here summarized as 'Acceptable').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether plans meet NIH expectations for data/material sharing; reviewers mark as Acceptable/Unacceptable and may comment on specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources: assessment of plans to authenticate key resources (here: 'Acceptable').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate whether the applicant provides adequate plans to validate identity and quality of biological/chemical resources (cell lines, antibodies, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support / Committee Budget Recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget and Period of Support: reviewers and committee provide recommendations regarding the requested budget (here: 'Recommend as Requested'). Administrative note: 'The budget shown is the requested budget and has not been adjusted to reflect any recommendations made by reviewers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee may recommend as requested or suggest modifications; grants management staff calculate final costs based on committee recommendations. The administrative note warns that the shown budget may be adjusted if an award is planned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Health Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Health Relevance: description of how the proposed research is relevant to public health and NIH mission (here: text explaining relevance to understanding epithelial immunity and potential impact on disease burden).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers (and NIH staff) use this to contextualize importance to public health; applicants should explicitly state relevance in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Process Scoring and Submission Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Process notes: 'The criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by the individual reviewers assigned to an application, and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies procedural aspects: criterion scores are entered before meeting, overall impact is discussed and scored by panel, overall score calculation described (average of overall scores * 10). Applicants should understand that criterion numeric scores do not directly compute the final Impact Score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and Communication Policy (Applicant Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of NIH Policy: applicant investigators and institutional officials must not communicate directly with study section members about an application before or after the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to observe this policy may create a breach of integrity in peer review and can lead to sanctions (including removal of the application from review) as described in NOT-OD-22-044. Also FOIA-related redaction considerations: reviewer comments and deliberations are protected and may be redacted in FOIA responses.
